t: Successor of Asturias, the kingdom took its name from León, the royal seat from 914, and ruled Galicia and the Douro plain.
Its kings claimed Visigothic heritage and an imperial title, and Alfonso VI captured Toledo in 1085.
The Cortes of León of 1188 included townsmen; in 1230 León was united permanently with Castile.
dyk: The Pantheon of the Kings at San Isidoro in León, burial place of Leonese royalty, preserves twelfth-century Romanesque wall paintings that include a calendar of the labours of the months.
ev: Alfonso III's sons divide his realm; García I rules from León
Ramiro II defeats Abd al-Rahman III at Simancas
Ferdinand I of Castile kills Bermudo III at Tamarón and takes León
Alfonso VII is crowned emperor in León
Alfonso IX summons the Cortes of León with town representatives
The Treaty of Benavente unites León with Castile under Ferdinand III
